requirement:
The harness MUST expose an `outline` tool with this interface:

```text
outline({ file: String }) -> Array<OutlineEntry>

OutlineEntry {
    item: String,
    kind: String,
    name: String?,
    children: Array<OutlineEntry>,
}
```

The tool MUST return the outline of a permitted file in a supported language
under {cite}`requirements.references.outlines`, with each node's selector under
{cite}`requirements.references.outline_selectors`, its kind, and its name when it
is named, nested by outline ancestry and in source order. Results MUST contain
no source text or line numbers and MUST NOT become evidence inputs; the model reads
the nodes it relies on with the `habeas` tool. For a file using the plain-text
profile, the outline lists its `line` nodes. Explicitly requesting an excluded
file MUST be handled as a denial under {cite}`requirements.authoring.read_denial`.
rationale:
The reviewed tests cover every obligation in `requirements.authoring.outline_tool`.

- **Interface.**
  - `tools.rs#mod[tests]/fn[outline_tool_is_advertised_with_a_required_file_argument]` asserts the advertised `outline` schema exactly: a string `file`, required, with no additional properties. It also checks that the description mentions the item selector, kind, name, no line numbers, no source text, and reading nodes with habeas.
  - `outline_lists_nested_nodes_without_text_or_inputs` asserts the exact result array for a Rust file. Each entry has `item`, `kind`, `name` and `children`.
  - The same test checks malformed arguments: a missing `file`, a non-string `file`, an extra argument, and a missing file. Each returns an explanatory error.
- **Selector, kind, name, nesting and order.** The Rust fixture has a struct followed by an impl whose child is `fn[run]`. The exact-equality assertion checks the selectors `struct[Thing]` and `impl[Thing]/fn[run]`, the kinds and names, nesting under the impl, and source order. Selector grammar details such as `#N` and percent-encoding belong to the cited `requirements.references.outline_selectors`. Per-language profiles belong to `requirements.references.outlines`. Neither is reassessed here.
- **No source text and no line numbers.**
  - The test asserts that the doc comment text "Docs" is absent from the serialized result.
  - It also asserts that no `line_start` key appears on plain-text entries, and the exact-equality assertion on the Rust result excludes any extra fields.
- **Not an evidence input.** `assert!(outline.inputs.is_empty())` covers this, and the outside-project test asserts that `recorded_inputs()` stays empty.
- **Plain-text profile.** `notes.txt` contains `alpha`, a blank line and `beta`. The test asserts two entries, each of kind `line`, with a null name and an `item` starting with `line@`. Blank lines are skipped.
- **Excluded file handled as a denial.**
  - The test adds `habeas.toml` with a disallow rule for `notes.txt`. It asserts a `PermissionDenied` error that names the path and says "disallowed", which gives the reason.
  - `unpermitted_requests_outside_the_project_are_recoverable_tool_errors` covers a path outside the project. It asserts a non-`PermissionDenied` recoverable error containing "outside the project". It then covers a matching disallow, which still returns `PermissionDenied`.
  - The searches I ran found further `outline` denial and read-failure cases. These include an untracked file under git, symlinks that leave the project, and book or target output.
- **`src/inputs.rs` tests.** The two `OutlineCache` tests are marked as tests of this requirement but only check cache sharing and override behaviour. They add nothing contradictory.

I found no obligation without a test and no assertion that contradicts the text. Every `MUST` is exercised and asserted.

text: :::{req} outline_tool
The harness MUST expose an `outline` tool with this interface:
```text
outline({ file: String }) -> Array<OutlineEntry>
OutlineEntry {
item: String,
kind: String,
name: String?,
children: Array<OutlineEntry>,
The tool MUST return the outline of a permitted file in a supported language
under {cite}`requirements.references.outlines`, with each node's selector under
{cite}`requirements.references.outline_selectors`, its kind, and its name when it
is named, nested by outline ancestry and in source order. Results MUST contain
no source text or line numbers and MUST NOT become evidence inputs; the model reads
the nodes it relies on with the `habeas` tool. For a file using the plain-text
profile, the outline lists its `line` nodes. Explicitly requesting an excluded
file MUST be handled as a denial under {cite}`requirements.authoring.read_denial`.
:::{req} outlines
Habeas MUST parse Rust, Python, TypeScript, CSS, Markdown, TOML, and YAML
sources with pinned tree-sitter grammars, selected by file extension compared
case-insensitively. A source with any syntax error MUST fail to parse, reporting
the line of its first error. Every
other text file MUST use a plain-text profile in which each line that is not
blank is an anonymous outline node of kind `line`. Each supported language MUST
have an outline profile that maps grammar node kinds to short outline kind names
and, for each mapped kind, states whether a node is named, and by which fields
or children, or anonymous. Only mapped kinds MUST appear in the outline, except
that a Markdown profile MAY additionally recognize colon-fenced directive
containers under {cite}`requirements.sdk.sources.markdown.fence_precedence`
and expose them as outline nodes under
{cite}`requirements.sdk.sources.markdown.fenced_blocks`. Such containers MUST
preserve source ranges and containment, and MUST NOT be recognized within
literal code or raw HTML. Other nodes MUST be transparent, so their outline
descendants appear under the nearest outline ancestor. A profile MAY attach grammar siblings to an outline
node, such as Rust attributes and doc comments preceding an item, so the outline
tree need not match the grammar tree exactly; attached siblings are part of that
node for its line range and hash. Every file's outline MUST have a root node
for the whole file, independent of language. Source in no other outline node,
such as top-level statements no profile maps, MUST belong to the root node;
profiles MUST NOT invent fallback kinds for it. Comments MUST NOT be outline nodes. Profiles MUST be
documented. Upgrading a grammar or profile MAY change outlines and MUST be
treated as a deliberate change.
:::{req} outline_selectors
An outline selector MUST be a `/`-separated path of segments from the file's
root node to an outline node; the empty selector MUST select the root node. A
named node's segment MUST be `kind[name]`. An anonymous node's segment MUST be
`kind@hash`, where `hash` is the first twelve hexadecimal digits of its identity
hash under {cite}`requirements.references.structural_hash`. Siblings whose
segments would otherwise be identical MUST be disambiguated by `#N`, their
one-based position among those siblings in source order, except `line` nodes:
identical lines are interchangeable, so a `line` selector MUST resolve when any
line with that content exists in the file. In names, `%`, `[`, `]`, `/`, `#`,
`@`, and whitespace MUST be percent-encoded as UTF-8 bytes, so selectors are
reversible. Line numbers MUST NOT form part of a selector.
:::{req} read_denial
When source-access policy denies a path that a model tool call names
explicitly, the harness MUST return a tool error naming the path and the reason
it cannot be read, add no evidence input, and continue the assessment.
Discovery and search MUST leave denied candidates out of their entries,
reporting untracked ones under {cite}`requirements.authoring.not_listed`. Malformed tool
arguments and ordinary read failures MUST also return explanatory tool errors.
